description: A new subcommand for an existing std-only Go CLI, farmctl (a solar farm's tool with list and read subcommands, a client for the plant SCADA gateway's line protocol that dials with no deadline, a fake gateway package for its tests, and docs/gateway.md, which says the gateway accepts at most 16 TCP connections at a time and closes any beyond that without a reply, holds a silent inverter's connection for up to 30 seconds, and takes a client that closes, or shuts down its sending side, as hanging up). The ticket asks for `farmctl yield`: every inverter's reading (300), one line each sorted by name as `read` prints it, inverters silent for 2 seconds as `no answer` and ERR replies with the gateway's code and text, a total line, exit 0/1/2, under a 15-second kill, within the gateway's documented connection limit. It names no technique. A sequential loop is correct and takes over 38 seconds. A goroutine per inverter, or a pool sized from the CPU count, is dropped past 16. A client that gives up on a read but leaves its connection open (a read raced against time.After in a select, since the existing client has no deadline), or only paces its reads, goes over 16 in the outage case, where more inverters are silent than the limit, whatever its own cap, while the program still exits on time. A client that keeps a silent inverter's connection open after giving up on it (a fixed pool of workers blocked on reads with no deadline while a collector moves on, ended by returning from main) stays within 16 and exits on time on an ordinary day, but holds each such connection for the gateway's 30 seconds, so in the outage the whole run waits on them. The check builds `go build ./cmd/farmctl` offline in bubblewrap; afterwards each case runs in its own sandbox with a hidden gateway inside its network namespace (hidden/driver.py; datasets and expected reports made in check.py and passed on standard input), on more than 16 CPUs (the run is invalid otherwise), so a pool sized from runtime.NumCPU is judged alike on every host that decides: a main case (300 inverters, some slow but within 2 s, some answering only after 3 to 6 s, some silent, some erroring), an all-answering case (36), an outage (300 inverters, 20 silent and 30 slow, all in the first third of both orders), no gateway, and list/read/usage against a small gateway. Required: builds, answered_inverters_correct (every answering inverter's line, sorted, in the main, all-answering, and outage cases), failures_handled (no-answer and error lines, total, exit 1 and 0, exit 2 within 10 s with no gateway), within_budget (the main case exits within max(15 s, 5x the best of up to three runs of a correct reference client timed in the same check), having asked for every inverter, and the outage within 5x the reference's time on it; the run is invalid when 5x the reference reaches the sequential floor; the main and all-answering cases are killed only at twice that floor, so a slow but correct client fails this check alone), within_limit (no connection refused in any case; at least one inverter asked), no_held_connections (no connection counted at the gateway longer than 8 s while the program ran, in any case; at least one inverter asked), no_work_after_exit (no connection in the 2 s after exit, no process left), existing_commands_unchanged (list, read, and usage errors as the fixture's tests expect, through the built program). Measures: seconds, peak and attempted connections, refusals, abandoned and held connections, the longest time a connection stayed counted (the reference client's too), connections open at exit, mean connections open, reads per inverter, the CPUs the program could use, the fixture's Go tests run against the agent's packages, the whole suite as the agent left it. Needs bubblewrap, python3 3.8 or later, the host's Go (TRIAL_GOROOT overrides it), and more than 16 CPUs; agent arms need Go readable only when it lives under the home.
prompt: Could you add a `farmctl yield` command? The Grafana agent will run it every minute to chart today's energy per inverter. It should read every inverter on the site (300 at the moment) and print one line each, sorted by inverter name, the same line `farmctl read` prints, then a last line like `total: 1034821 Wh from 297 of 300 inverters` (the sum over the inverters that gave a reading). Some inverters are always dark (tripped, or a dead comms card) and the gateway just holds the connection open on those, so one that hasn't answered within 2 seconds should print as `INV-117: no answer`; if the gateway answers with an error, print it with the gateway's code and text, like `INV-117: error 503 inverter fault`. Exit 0 when every inverter gave a reading, 1 otherwise, and 2 when the inverter list can't be read. The agent kills a command that runs longer than 15 seconds. And please respect the gateway's connection limit in docs/gateway.md; going over it trips an alarm in the control room.
